title: Natural comparison conjugation preserves tower squares, units and scalar localization
statement:
Let $\mathcal D_0,\mathcal D_1,\mathcal D_2$ be categories [def-nagata-category]. For $0\leq i<j\leq2$, let $T_{ji},B_{ji}:\mathcal D_i\to\mathcal D_j$ be functors and $\chi_{ji}:T_{ji}\xrightarrow{\sim}B_{ji}$ natural isomorphisms. Let $W_i:\mathcal D_i\to\mathcal D_i$ be functors, $\alpha_{ji}:T_{ji}W_i\xrightarrow{\sim}W_jT_{ji}$ natural isomorphisms, and $\mu:T_{21}T_{10}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{20}$ a natural isomorphism. Functors preserve identities and composition; a natural isomorphism is a family of invertible arrows commuting with every morphism. Composition below is read right to left, with functor associators understood. Suppose
$$W_2(\mu_K)\circ\alpha_{21,T_{10}K}\circ T_{21}(\alpha_{10,K})=\alpha_{20,K}\circ\mu_{W_0K}.$$
Put
$$d_K=\chi_{21,B_{10}K}\circ T_{21}(\chi_{10,K}),\quad a_K=\chi_{20,K}\circ\mu_K\circ d_K^{-1},\quad\beta_{ji,K}=W_j(\chi_{ji,K})\circ\alpha_{ji,K}\circ\chi_{ji,W_iK}^{-1}.$$
These are natural isomorphisms and satisfy
$$W_2(a_K)\circ\beta_{21,B_{10}K}\circ B_{21}(\beta_{10,K})=\beta_{20,K}\circ a_{W_0K}.$$
More precisely, the normalization of its two paths is
$$\beta_{21,B_{10}K}\circ B_{21}(\beta_{10,K})\circ d_{W_0K}=W_2(d_K)\circ\alpha_{21,T_{10}K}\circ T_{21}(\alpha_{10,K}),$$
$$\beta_{20,K}\circ a_{W_0K}\circ d_{W_0K}=W_2(\chi_{20,K})\circ\alpha_{20,K}\circ\mu_{W_0K}.$$
For identity transitions include $T_{ii},B_{ii}$ and $\chi_{ii}$, and a natural unit $u_i:T_{ii}\xrightarrow{\sim}1$. Set $v_i=u_i\circ\chi_{ii}^{-1}:B_{ii}\to1$. If $W_i(u_{i,K})\circ\alpha_{ii,K}=u_{i,W_iK}$ and the ordinary associators with repeated adjacent indices are $T_{ji}(u_i)$ and $u_jT_{ji}$, respectively, their transported versions satisfy $W_i(v_{i,K})\circ\beta_{ii,K}=v_{i,W_iK}$ and are $B_{ji}(v_i)$ and $v_jB_{ji}$.

Suppose additionally that $A_0\to A_1\to A_2$ are commutative rings, $t_i\in A_i$, each $\mathcal D_i$ is $A_i$-linear [def-weil-linear-category], each transition functor $F:\mathcal D_i\to\mathcal D_j$ is additive and semilinear for the ring map $\varphi:A_i\to A_j$ (for $j=2$, $i=0$ the composite $A_0\to A_1\to A_2$), that is $F(f+g)=F(f)+F(g)$ and $F(af)=\varphi(a)F(f)$ for $a\in A_i$, and $W_i$ is $A_i$-linear [def-weil-linear-functor]. Assume the images of $t_i$ are invertible in $A_j[1/t_j]$ for $i<j$. In the raw scalar localizations [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization], every comparison above extends with components equal to its image under the localization functor. All displayed equations and inverse and unit equations remain true; localization of $a$ is exactly the transport of localized $\mu$ through localized $\chi$. The extensions are natural for every localized morphism $f\otimes s$, and thus for its finite sums, not only for integral morphisms. No faithfulness of scalar localization is asserted.

proof.text: First note the elementary natural-transformation rules used below. If $\eta:F\to G$ and $\theta:G\to H$ are natural, then $H(f)\theta_X\eta_X=\theta_YG(f)\eta_X=\theta_Y\eta_YF(f)$; their composite is natural. Applying a functor to this equation gives naturality after postcomposition, and evaluating it on the image of an arrow gives naturality after precomposition. Multiplying $G(f)\eta_X=\eta_YF(f)$ by the component inverses gives $F(f)\eta_X^{-1}=\eta_Y^{-1}G(f)$. Functors preserve inverse equations since they preserve identities and composition. Consequently $d,a,\beta$ and $v_i$ are natural with invertible components, by their displayed formulas. These calculations use only the definition of natural isomorphism in the statement and the category laws of [def-nagata-category].

proof.text:
Fix $K$ and abbreviate $F=T_{21}$, $G=B_{21}$, $P=T_{10}$, $Q=B_{10}$, $c=\chi_{21}$, $e=\chi_{10}$, $A=\alpha_{21}$, $b=\alpha_{10}$, $U=W_0$, $V=W_1$, $W=W_2$. Composition is still right to left. Naturality of $c$ at $\beta_{10,K}:Q(UK)\to V(QK)$ gives
$$c_{VQK}^{-1}G(\beta_{10,K})c_{QUK}=F(\beta_{10,K}).$$
Expand the definition of $\beta_{21,QK}$ and $d_{UK}$, use this equality, then cancel $F(e_{UK}^{-1})F(e_{UK})$:
$$\begin{aligned}
\beta_{21,QK}G(\beta_{10,K})d_{UK}
&=W(c_{QK})A_{QK}F(\beta_{10,K})F(e_{UK})\\
&=W(c_{QK})A_{QK}F(V(e_K))F(b_K).
\end{aligned}$$
Naturality of $A$ at $e_K:PK\to QK$ says $A_{QK}F(V(e_K))=W(F(e_K))A_{PK}$. The last expression is therefore $W(d_K)A_{PK}F(b_K)$, exactly the first required normalization. Only naturality, the functor laws and the associative/inverse laws of [def-nagata-category] were used.

proof.text:
For an identity transition, substitute the definitions and use the assumed unit compatibility:
$$\begin{aligned}
W_i(v_{i,K})\beta_{ii,K}
&=W_i(u_{i,K})W_i(\chi_{ii,K}^{-1})W_i(\chi_{ii,K})\alpha_{ii,K}\chi_{ii,W_iK}^{-1}\\
&=u_{i,W_iK}\chi_{ii,W_iK}^{-1}=v_{i,W_iK}.
\end{aligned}$$
The inverse factors cancel by the functor and category laws of [def-nagata-category].

proof.text:
For repeated indices use the same definition of transported associator, with the repeated-index ordinary associators specified in the hypothesis. For $(j,i,i)$ it gives, on $K\in\mathcal D_i$,
$$\begin{aligned}
a_{jii,K}&=\chi_{ji,K}T_{ji}(u_{i,K})T_{ji}(\chi_{ii,K}^{-1})\chi_{ji,B_{ii}K}^{-1}\\
&=\chi_{ji,K}T_{ji}(v_{i,K})\chi_{ji,B_{ii}K}^{-1}=B_{ji}(v_{i,K}),
\end{aligned}$$
where the final equality is naturality of $\chi_{ji}$ at $v_{i,K}:B_{ii}K\to K$. For $(j,j,i)$ it gives
$$a_{jji,K}=\chi_{ji,K}u_{j,T_{ji}K}T_{jj}(\chi_{ji,K}^{-1})\chi_{jj,B_{ji}K}^{-1}
=u_{j,B_{ji}K}\chi_{jj,B_{ji}K}^{-1}=v_{j,B_{ji}K},$$
using naturality of $u_j:T_{jj}\to1$ at $\chi_{ji,K}:T_{ji}K\to B_{ji}K$. Thus both asserted unit degeneracies hold, also if all indices coincide. This is substitution and the category laws [def-nagata-category], without any further coherence assumption.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization] to every $T_{ji},B_{ji}$, taking $R=A_i$, $S=A_j$, $t=t_i$, $u=t_j$ and the specified coefficient map. Its unit-image hypothesis is exactly the assumed invertibility in $A_j[1/t_j]$. For $W_i$ and the identity transition functors use the identity coefficient map; $t_i$ is already invertible in $A_i[1/t_i]$. Linearity of $W_i$ includes additivity by [def-weil-linear-functor]. The cited localization lemma extends each functor and every natural isomorphism, with components $Q_j$ of its original components; it preserves identities, vertical composition and whiskering. Hence the localized definitions of $d,a,\beta,v$ are precisely the definitions using the extended functors and comparisons. Localized inverse components are the images of the integral inverses. Apply its equation-preservation assertion to the tower, both normalizations, inverse equations and the unit equations proved above. In particular $\overline a=\overline\chi_{20}\,\overline\mu\,\overline d^{-1}$ is exactly transport of localized $\mu$ through localized $\chi$. No triangle or exactness clause of the localization lemma is used.

proof.text:
To make naturality on the full raw localization explicit, let $\eta:F\Rightarrow G$ be any comparison in the preceding step between functors with the same coefficient map $\varphi:A_i\to A_j$, and write $\bar\varphi:A_i[1/t_i]\to A_j[1/t_j]$ for its extension. The fraction formula of [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization] and semilinearity give
$$\bar F(f\otimes s)=Q_j(F(f))\bar\varphi(s),\qquad
\bar G(f\otimes s)=Q_j(G(f))\bar\varphi(s).$$
Using integral naturality and bilinearity of composition [def-weil-linear-category],
$$\bar G(f\otimes s)Q_j(\eta_K)
=\bar\varphi(s)Q_j(G(f)\eta_K)
=\bar\varphi(s)Q_j(\eta_LF(f))
=Q_j(\eta_L)\bar F(f\otimes s).$$
Every morphism in the tensor Hom module of [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization] is a finite sum of pure tensors, so additivity extends this equality to all arrows. For the composite transition the coefficient maps agree because the $0\to2$ map is the composite; for $\alpha,\beta$ the $W_i$ have identity coefficient map. Thus this calculation applies to every comparison, including their inverses and units. Equalities were only mapped forward by $Q_j$; faithfulness is unnecessary.
